# Intraday volume asymmetry: development report

**Family:** `family-volume-skew` (reserve family). Primary mechanism: the
asymmetry of QQQ's intraday volume distribution is a fragility state; hold
TQQQ for the next session when down-volume dominates its recent distribution,
stay in cash when up-volume dominance is crowded.

**Verdict: passes every kill criterion, including the above-TQQQ CAGR bar at
1 bp: 42.02% CAGR vs 36.72%, with a 34.84% max drawdown vs 82.29% and Sharpe
1.21 vs 0.82. The honest caveats are that the headline is sensitive to 2020
(ex-2020 CAGR 34.16%, just below the bar), the signal is partly a volume-
weighted short-term reversal (0.450 correlation with `family-short-reversal`),
and 10 bp costs cut CAGR to 19.33%. It is the strongest of the three reserve
families.**

Development window 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 1-minute marks, next-open fills,
2% band, long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. The panel is requested with
`end=2023-12-29`; no 2024-2026 bar is used. The signal uses QQQ minute volume;
the position is TQQQ.

---

## 1. Headline

| | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Bar-time exposure | Fills | Turnover | Ending equity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Primary, 1 bp** | **42.02%** | **34.84%** | **1.21** | **1.73** | 34.0% | 38.41% | 1,544 | 7,237x | $1,645,749 |
| Primary, 2 bp | 39.30% | 35.23% | 1.15 | 1.64 | 34.0% | 38.41% | 1,544 | 6,487x | $1,410,291 |
| Primary, 5 bp | 31.45% | 36.39% | 0.98 | 1.40 | 34.0% | 38.41% | 1,544 | 4,718x | $887,449 |
| Primary, 10 bp | 19.33% | 42.32% | 0.69 | 0.99 | 34.0% | 38.41% | 1,544 | 2,876x | $410,079 |
| Primary, 0 bp (gross) | 44.79% | 34.45% | 1.26 | 1.81 | 34.0% | 38.41% | 1,544 | 8,086x | $1,920,519 |
| TQQQ buy & hold (sim) | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1.12 | 66.5% | 100% | 1 | 1x | $1,175,283 |
| TQQQ bar from the brief | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 | -- | -- | 100% | -- | -- | -- |

- At 1 bp the strategy is **+5.30 pp above** the TQQQ CAGR bar and cuts max
  drawdown by **47.5 pp** (34.84% vs 82.29%). Sharpe is 1.21 vs 0.82.
- At 2 bp it is still above the bar (+2.58 pp). At 5 bp it is 5.27 pp below
  (31.45%); at 10 bp it is 19.33%. The result is cost-sensitive because the
  book trades every held day.
- Exposure is **38.41% of 1-minute bars** and **10.5% of calendar time**
  (781 signals, 772 events, day session only). The rest is cash.
- Daily correlation to TQQQ is **0.489**. This is a high-exposure TQQQ
  strategy, not a small sleeve; the drawdown reduction comes from being out of
  the worst sessions.
- Max drawdown episode: **2022-01-19 -> 2022-04-25, 34.84%**. The strategy
  still finished 2022 at +25.5%; the drawdown is an early-year giveback.

---

## 2. What it is

Universe: QQQ (signal), TQQQ (position), cash.

At 15:59 ET on session `d`:

```
U_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close > open)
D_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close < open)
A_d = (U_d - D_d) / (U_d + D_d)
ref_d = 40th percentile of A over the prior 60 full sessions
```

If `A_d < ref_d`, buy TQQQ at the next session's **09:30 open** and sell at
that session's **15:59 open**. Otherwise hold cash. No overnight position.

**Clock.** The signal is fixed at 15:59:00 on `d`, after all 390 bars are
complete. The reference uses `d-60 .. d-1` only; the current value is excluded.
The entry is the next 09:30 open; the exit is the next 15:59 open (target zero
at the 15:58 close). There is no same-bar fill and no future data.

Only 390-bar sessions are eligible. Half-days are skipped; they still update
the previous close.

---

## 3. Event statistics

772 events over 8 years, **96.7 events/year**. Per-event TQQQ return, next
09:30 open to next 15:59 open:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Events | 772 |
| Mean | **+44.1 bp** |
| Median | +50.1 bp |
| Win rate | 58.4% |
| t-stat | **3.60** |
| Worst | -1,237.4 bp |
| Best | +2,146.7 bp |
| Sum of log returns | +2.955 |

The mean is supported by the median and the win rate; the t-stat is 3.60. The
best event is +21.5% and the worst -12.4%, both real TQQQ day moves.

---

## 4. Why the signal, not price, volume level or volatility

| Control | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | What it says |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Volume asymmetry < q0.40** | **42.02%** | **34.84%** | **1.21** | 1,544 | The strategy. |
| Breadth (equal-weight up/down bars) < q0.40 | 31.22% | 30.70% | 0.98 | 1,528 | Volume weighting adds 10.8 pp CAGR and 0.23 Sharpe over an equal-weight count. |
| Price-only return < q0.40 | 9.78% | 62.35% | 0.45 | 1,554 | The signal is not just "buy after a down day". |
| Total volume < q0.40 | 6.73% | 48.08% | 0.38 | 1,686 | Volume level is not the driver. |
| Realized 5-min vol < q0.40 | -2.78% | 59.73% | 0.01 | 1,698 | Volatility is not the driver. |
| Top-5% volume concentration < q0.40 | -4.28% | 68.30% | 0.06 | 1,486 | Concentration is not the driver. |
| Minute-volume skew < q0.40 | -0.42% | 68.99% | 0.16 | 1,554 | Distribution skew alone is not the driver. |
| Stale signal | 5.80% | 70.44% | 0.34 | 1,536 | The same-day volume is doing the work. |
| All full sessions, day-only | 2.40% | 71.52% | 0.30 | 3,938 | TQQQ's return is mostly overnight; the day-only book is not beta. |
| Buy & hold TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1 | The absolute-return bar. |

The controls are decisive: the price-only version earns 9.78% with a 62.4%
drawdown, the volume-level version 6.73%, and the realized-vol version -2.78%.
The volume asymmetry is the object doing the work. The breadth control is the
closest competitor at 31.22% / 30.70% / 0.98; the volume weighting is what
lifts the strategy above the TQQQ bar.

The continuation sign is a strong negative control: holding when `A` is above
its 60th percentile earns **-19.31% CAGR with an 89.8% drawdown** (Sharpe
-0.60). The fragility direction is the right one in this sample.

---

## 5. Robustness

### 5.1 Pre-registered grid (8 cells)

All cells use the next-session 09:30 -> 15:59 clock and TQQQ 1.0. The centre is
cell 6.

| Cell | Lookback | Percentile | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | 1 bp Sharpe | 5 bp CAGR | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 20 | 0.30 | 28.77% | 36.43% | 0.99 | 21.22% | 1,206 |
| 2 | 20 | 0.40 | 41.04% | 44.26% | 1.19 | 30.37% | 1,570 |
| 3 | 40 | 0.30 | 38.20% | 34.72% | 1.22 | 30.17% | 1,196 |
| 4 | 40 | 0.40 | 41.93% | 33.06% | 1.20 | 31.30% | 1,554 |
| 5 | 60 | 0.30 | 35.69% | 33.73% | 1.15 | 27.93% | 1,176 |
| **6** | **60** | **0.40** | **42.02%** | **34.84%** | **1.21** | **31.45%** | **1,544** |
| 7 | 100 | 0.30 | 30.04% | 30.29% | 1.01 | 22.79% | 1,146 |
| 8 | 100 | 0.40 | 32.18% | 34.84% | 0.99 | 22.36% | 1,540 |

**8/8 cells are positive at 1 bp and 8/8 at 5 bp.** The 1 bp CAGR range is
28.8% to 42.0%; 4 of 8 cells are above the 36.72% TQQQ bar at 1 bp. The 20/0.30
cell is the weak spot (28.77%). The plateau is broad in sign and level, and the
centre is not a knife-edge: 40/0.40 is nearly identical.

### 5.2 Neighbours (not used to choose the centre)

| Neighbour | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | Sharpe | 5 bp CAGR | 10 bp CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q 0.35 | 40.82% | 35.10% | 1.22 | 31.57% | 20.86% |
| q 0.45 | 34.84% | 38.14% | 1.01 | 23.46% | 10.58% |
| Look 30 | 36.83% | 32.50% | 1.09 | 26.57% | 14.82% |
| Look 80 | 38.05% | 35.00% | 1.12 | 27.69% | 15.82% |
| Look 120 | 33.27% | 35.46% | 1.02 | 23.44% | 12.16% |
| Hold 2 sessions | 29.54% | 54.25% | 0.83 | 14.29% | -2.27% |
| Size 0.50 | 20.96% | 17.94% | 1.21 | 16.34% | 10.83% |
| QQQ execution | 12.61% | 12.84% | 1.12 | 4.23% | -5.38% |

The result is stable to the percentile (0.35-0.45) and the lookback (30-120).
A two-session hold is much worse (29.54% CAGR, 54.25% DD), so the effect is a
one-session rebalancing, not a persistent regime. QQQ execution has the same
Sharpe (1.12) with a much lower drawdown (12.84%), confirming that TQQQ is a
capital-efficiency choice.

### 5.3 Placebo

| Placebo | Draws | Real CAGR | Placebo mean | Placebo p95 | Max | p-value | Real DD percentile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Random days, same count, same clock | 200 | 42.02% | 1.48% | 14.45% | 23.59% | **0.000** | 100.0% |

The real result beats all 200 random-day draws; the best random draw is
23.59% CAGR, 18.4 pp below the strategy. The real drawdown is better than
every random draw. The volume asymmetry is selecting the days, not riding beta.

### 5.4 Subperiods and yearly

| Period | CAGR | Max DD |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 19.80% | 29.54% |
| 2020-2021 | 84.04% | 24.59% |
| 2022-2023 | 54.36% | 34.84% |

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +33.53% | +19.86% |
| 2017 | +38.42% | +114.54% |
| 2018 | **-8.32%** | -20.76% |
| 2019 | +21.71% | +148.23% |
| 2020 | **+111.86%** | +104.14% |
| 2021 | +59.55% | +81.05% |
| 2022 | +25.48% | -79.39% |
| 2023 | +88.70% | +192.05% |

The strategy is positive in 7 of 8 calendar years and all 3 subperiods. 2018
is the only loss (-8.3%). 2020 is the dominant year (+111.9%) and the reason
the headline is above the TQQQ bar; the report does not hide that.

### 5.5 Cut tests

| Cut | Strategy CAGR | Strategy DD | TQQQ ex-year CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ex-2016 | 43.28% | 32.98% | 38.66% |
| ex-2017 | 42.60% | 32.98% | 27.06% |
| ex-2018 | 51.21% | 32.98% | 46.60% |
| ex-2019 | 45.22% | 35.76% | 25.90% |
| ex-2020 | **34.16%** | 32.98% | 27.84% |
| ex-2021 | 39.70% | 35.83% | 30.34% |
| ex-2022 | 44.56% | 26.74% | 77.75% |
| ex-2023 | 36.33% | 32.98% | 21.49% |

No single year carries the result: the cut range is 34.16% to 51.21%.
**Excluding 2020 lowers CAGR to 34.16%, just below the 36.72% bar**, while
Sharpe remains around 1.0. The above-TQQQ claim is therefore sensitive to the
2020 rebound year; the strategy is still a strong risk-adjusted performer
without it.

---

## 6. Correlation to the nine current winners

Daily returns, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 2,011 overlapping days.

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.357 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.456 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.469 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.347 |
| family-session-timing | 0.231 |
| family-short-reversal | **0.450** |
| family-rebalance-flow | **0.514** |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.320 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.441 |

Range **0.231 .. 0.514**, below the 0.70 independence gate. The highest
correlation is with `family-rebalance-flow` (0.514); the short-reversal
correlation is 0.450. The signal is a volume-weighted reversal/fragility
measure, so this overlap is expected. Extra archive correlations:
`overnight-drift-filter` 0.463, `family-volume-clock` 0.127,
`family-realized-skew` 0.430, `family-gap-continuation` 0.158.

---

## 7. Kill criteria

| Criterion | Value | Failed? |
|---|---:|---|
| 1 bp CAGR below 36.72% TQQQ bar | 42.02% | **pass** |
| 5 bp CAGR below 0 | 31.45% | pass |
| Fewer than 30 independent events | 772 | pass |
| Fewer than 100 fills | 1,544 | pass |
| Fewer than 6/8 grid cells positive at 1 bp | 8/8 | pass |
| Negative CAGR in 2+ of 3 subperiods | 0 of 3 | pass |
| Placebo random-day p-value > 0.10 | 0.000 | pass |
| Correlation > 0.70 with a winner | 0.514 | pass |
| Weight drift before a truncation cut | 0.0 | pass |

**All nine criteria pass.** This is the only one of the three reserve families
that clears the above-TQQQ CAGR bar.

---

## 8. Risks and limitations

1. **2020 dependence.** Ex-2020 CAGR is 34.16%, below the 36.72% bar. The
   headline above-TQQQ claim depends on the 2020 rebound. The strategy is still
   positive and high-Sharpe without it, but the margin is thin.
2. **Reversal overlap.** The signal is a volume-weighted breadth measure. The
   same-day price/return correlation is 0.476, and the correlation with
   `family-short-reversal` is 0.450. The price-only control (9.78%) and the
   equal-weight breadth control (31.22%) show that volume weighting adds
   materially, but this is not an independent factor. It passes the 0.70 gate.
3. **Cost sensitivity.** At 5 bp CAGR is 31.45% (below the bar); at 10 bp it is
   19.33%. Turnover is 7,237x initial equity over 8 years (~900x/yr). A real
   implementation with market impact above the flat-bps model would erode the
   edge.
4. **2018 loss.** The only negative year is 2018 (-8.3%), with a 62% drawdown
   in the price-only control but a 34.8% max DD in the strategy. A sustained
   choppy market is the weak regime.
5. **TQQQ 3x.** The book is 100% TQQQ on 38% of days. The 2% band and 1 bp cost
   model do not capture a gap through a stop; there is no stop. The QQQ
   execution variant has a much lower drawdown (12.84%) and the same Sharpe
   (1.12), which is the conservative implementation.
6. **Volume data.** QQQ minute volume is unadjusted for splits, but the
   signal is a within-day ratio, so splits cancel. The 2016-2020 archive has
   occasional after-hours prints; `bt.load_1m` filters to 09:30-16:00 and
   half-days after 13:00. The result survives lookbacks of 20-120 sessions.

---

## 9. Verdict

**Pass on every kill criterion, including the above-TQQQ CAGR bar at 1 bp.**
The intraday up/down volume asymmetry is a real fragility signal in this
sample: low asymmetry days earn +44.1 bp per next session (t = 3.60), the
continuation sign loses 19.3% CAGR, and the price-only, volume-level and
realized-vol controls are far weaker. The strategy is a volume-weighted
reversal/fragility book, not a pure independent factor; its 0.450 correlation
with `family-short-reversal` and its 2020 dependence are the reasons to treat
it as a strong reserve/winner candidate rather than a guaranteed replacement
for TQQQ. At 1 bp it is the best of the three reserve families and the only one
that clears the programme's absolute-return bar.
hypothesis_md:
# Intraday volume asymmetry: hypothesis and pre-registration

**Family:** `family-volume-skew` (reserve family).

**One-line hypothesis.** The asymmetry of the intraday volume distribution is
a fragility signal. When up-volume dominates the session, the move is crowded
and the next session tends to give some of it back; when down-volume dominates
and the asymmetry is in the lower part of its recent distribution, supply has
been absorbed and the next session is more balanced. A long-only TQQQ book can
hold the second state and sit in cash in the first.

**Development window.** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. The shared 1-minute
panel and QQQ minute volume are requested with `end=2023-12-29`; no 2024-2026
bar enters any signal, weight or statistic. The holdout is not loaded.

---

## 1. Why this should exist

Volume is not just activity; it says who is doing the trading. A session with
heavy up-volume is a crowded demand state: the marginal buyer has already
acted, and the next session is more vulnerable to profit-taking. A session
with heavy down-volume is a supply-absorption state: sellers have been filled,
and the next session can be more balanced. This is a *fragility* hypothesis,
not a volume-level or volume-acceleration hypothesis.

The primary object is the **up-volume versus down-volume asymmetry**:

```
U_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close > open)
D_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close < open)
A_d = (U_d - D_d) / (U_d + D_d)
```

`A_d` is scale-free and split-invariant. It is not the volume level (total
volume), not volume acceleration (a short/long volume ratio), and not
volatility (realized variance). The controls in the report separate all three.

The signal is deliberately **not**:

- a trend gate (no moving average, no 100-250 day filter);
- volatility targeting (size is 0 or 1);
- a drawdown/capitulation event;
- a calendar/FOMC/OpEx window;
- opening-range, close-flow, ML or relative-strength.

## 2. Exact rules

All times US/Eastern. Bar offsets are 0-based from 09:30 (0) to 15:59 (389).

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Signal asset | QQQ |
| Trade asset | TQQQ (3x QQQ), weight 1.0; cash otherwise |
| Signal | `A_d = (up-volume - down-volume) / (up + down)` |
| Reference | 40th percentile of `A` over the prior 60 full sessions |
| Entry condition | `A_d < ref_d` (lower part of its recent distribution) |
| Entry | next session 09:30 open |
| Exit | next session 15:59 open (target zero at the 15:58 close) |
| Hold | one session, no overnight position |
| Short side | not traded (long-only book) |

**Decision clock.** The signal is fixed at 15:59:00 on session `d`, after all
390 one-minute bars are complete. The reference uses sessions `d-60 .. d-1`
only (a one-session shift; the current value is not in the reference). The
entry is the next session's 09:30 open; the exit is that session's 15:59 open.
There is no same-bar fill and no future data.

Only sessions with 390 one-minute bars are eligible. Half-days are skipped;
they still update the previous close.

## 3. Pre-registered centre and grid

Centre: **60-session reference, 40th percentile, TQQQ 1.0, one-session hold.**

The 8-cell grid varies the reference window and the percentile:

| Cell | Lookback | Percentile |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 20 | 0.30 |
| 2 | 20 | 0.40 |
| 3 | 40 | 0.30 |
| 4 | 40 | 0.40 |
| 5 | 60 | 0.30 |
| 6 | **60** | **0.40** (centre) |
| 7 | 100 | 0.30 |
| 8 | 100 | 0.40 |

The centre selects about 38% of sessions. The 60-session window is long enough
to estimate a distribution and short enough to adapt to a changing volume
regime. The grid is reported in full and the centre is allowed to be non-best.

## 4. Kill criteria (stated before the confirmatory run)

Primary performance is the 1 bp headline. The strategy must also survive
5 bp and 10 bp. A candidate is killed if any of the following holds:

1. Dev CAGR at 1 bp is below the 36.72% TQQQ development bar.
2. 5 bp CAGR is below zero.
3. Fewer than 30 independent events or fewer than 100 fills.
4. Fewer than 6 of 8 grid cells have positive 1 bp CAGR.
5. Negative CAGR in 2 or more of the 3 subperiods (2016-19, 2020-21, 2022-23).
6. Placebo random-day p-value above 0.10.
7. Daily-return correlation above 0.70 with any of the nine current winners.
8. Any weight drift before a truncation cut.

Criterion 1 is the programme's absolute-return bar. Criteria 2-8 are
robustness and integrity gates.

## 5. Placebos and controls

- **Random days:** draw the same number of full sessions at random, keep the
  next-session 09:30 -> 15:59 clock. 200 draws. This asks whether the volume
  asymmetry selects better days than the calendar.
- **Stale signal:** use the previous session's flag. This asks whether the
  same-day volume is doing the work.
- **Price-only reversal:** hold when the same-day QQQ return is below its
  prior-60-session 40th percentile. This asks whether the signal is just
  "buy after a down day".
- **Breadth:** the same rule using the count of up versus down bars, equal
  weight, instead of volume. This asks whether volume weighting matters.
- **Volume level, realized volatility, top-5 volume concentration,
  minute-volume skew:** each below its prior-60-session 40th percentile. These
  ask whether the primary object is just volume, volatility, concentration, or
  a different skew.
- **Continuation sign:** hold when `A` is above its 60th percentile. This asks
  whether the sign is the one the fragility hypothesis predicts.

## 6. What would falsify the hypothesis

- The price-only or breadth control earning as much would mean the volume
  asymmetry adds nothing.
- The volume-level or realized-vol control earning as much would mean the
  family is a volume/volatility proxy, not a skew signal.
- The continuation sign earning as much would mean the fragility direction is
  wrong.
- A random-day placebo matching the real result would mean the edge is
  calendar drift.
- A stale signal keeping the result would mean the same-day volume is
  irrelevant.

## 7. Design disclosure

The 60-session/40th-percentile centre was fixed during development after a
small scan of lookbacks and percentiles. The grid shows a broad positive
plateau; the centre is the best 1 bp cell at the 60-session window, and the
40-session/40th-percentile cell is nearly identical (41.93% CAGR, 33.06% DD).
The contrarian sign was tested against the continuation sign: the
continuation version loses money (-19.3% CAGR, 89.8% DD at the 60th
percentile), so the report frames the family as a **fragility** signal, not a
continuation signal. This sign choice is data-driven and is disclosed. The
same-day price/volume correlation is 0.476, so the signal is partly a
short-term reversal; the price-only and breadth controls quantify how much the
volume asymmetry adds.

"""Intraday volume-asymmetry fragility: hold TQQQ after down-volume dominance.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded.

Family
------
`family-volume-skew` (reserve family).  Primary object: the asymmetry of the
intraday volume distribution, measured as up-volume versus down-volume on
QQQ one-minute bars.  This is not volume level, volume acceleration, or
volatility.

Hypothesis
----------
Volume carries information about who is doing the trading.  When up-volume
dominates the session, the move is crowded and fragile; the next session tends
to give some of it back.  When down-volume dominates and the asymmetry sits in
the lower part of its recent distribution, the session has already absorbed
supply and the next session is more balanced.  A long-only TQQQ book can hold
the second state and sit in cash in the first.

Rules
-----
For each full 390-bar QQQ session d:

    U_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close > open)
    D_d = sum(volume of 1-min bars with close < open)
    A_d = (U_d - D_d) / (U_d + D_d)          in [-1, 1]

    ref_d = 40th percentile of A over the prior 60 full sessions
            (strictly before d; no current-session value in the reference)

    A_d < ref_d  -> hold TQQQ for the next session,
                    buy at the next 09:30 open, sell at the next 15:59 open.
    otherwise    -> cash.

Decision clock: 15:59:00 ET, after the close of session d.  The entry is the
next session's 09:30 open; the exit is that session's 15:59 open (target zero
at the 15:58 close).  No overnight position, no same-bar fill.

No trend gate, volatility target, drawdown event, calendar window, ML or
relative-strength input.  The only signal is volume asymmetry.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/strategies/family-volume-skew/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BPY = 252 * 390
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")
CQ, CT, CB = 0, 1, 2
N_BARS = 390

# Pre-registered centre.
LOOK = 60             # prior-session reference window
Q = 0.40              # hold when A is below its 40th percentile
HOLD = 1              # next session only
EXIT_OFF = 389        # 15:59 open

WINNERS = [
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
]
EXTRA_CURVES = [
    "overnight-drift-filter", "family-volume-clock", "family-realized-skew",
    "family-gap-continuation", "family-close-location",
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# data / signal
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def load_panel(start: str = DEV_START, end: str = DEV_END):
    return bt.panel(SYMBOLS, start, end, "1min", warmup_days=0)


def skewness(x: np.ndarray) -> float:
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    m = x.mean()
    s = x.std()
    return float(((x - m) ** 3).mean() / s ** 3) if s > 0 else np.nan


def daily_volume_features(ts):
    """Per-session QQQ volume asymmetry and diagnostic volume features."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    sess = pd.to_datetime(dates[first])
    n = len(first)
    q = bt.load_1m("QQQ")
    q = q[(q["date"] >= pd.Timestamp(DEV_START).date())
          & (q["date"] <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END).date())].copy()
    q["up"] = q["close"] > q["open"]
    q["dn"] = q["close"] < q["open"]

    g = q.groupby("date")
    daily = g.agg(vol=("volume", "sum"), nb=("close", "size"),
                  nup=("up", "sum"), ndn=("dn", "sum"),
                  close=("close", "last"))
    daily.index = pd.to_datetime(daily.index)
    daily = daily.reindex(sess)

    up = q[q["up"]].groupby("date")["volume"].sum()
    dn = q[q["dn"]].groupby("date")["volume"].sum()
    up.index = pd.to_datetime(up.index)
    dn.index = pd.to_datetime(dn.index)
    up = up.reindex(sess).fillna(0.0)
    dn = dn.reindex(sess).fillna(0.0)

    daily["upvol"] = up
    daily["dnvol"] = dn
    daily["asym"] = (up - dn) / (up + dn).replace(0, np.nan)
    daily["breadth"] = (daily["nup"] - daily["ndn"]) / (daily["nup"] + daily["ndn"])
    top5 = g["volume"].apply(
        lambda x: (np.sort(np.asarray(x, dtype=float))[::-1][:max(1, int(0.05 * len(x)))].sum()
                   / np.sum(x)) if np.sum(x) > 0 else np.nan)
    top5.index = pd.to_datetime(top5.index)
    daily["top5"] = top5.reindex(sess)
    vskew = g["volume"].apply(lambda x: skewness(np.asarray(x, dtype=float)))
    vskew.index = pd.to_datetime(vskew.index)
    daily["vol_skew"] = vskew.reindex(sess)
    return daily, sess


def volume_features_from_panel(ts, o, c):
    """Volume features plus a panel-based 5-minute realized-vol control."""
    daily, sess = daily_volume_features(ts)
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    rv = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for k in range(n):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        if l - f != N_BARS - 1:
            continue
        px = c[f:l + 1, CQ]
        c5 = px[4::5]
        if len(c5) >= 10:
            r5 = np.diff(np.log(c5))
            rv[k] = float(np.std(r5))
    daily["rv"] = rv
    return daily, sess


def signal_flags(daily, full, look: int = LOOK, q: float = Q):
    """Hold flags for the next session, using only prior-session quantiles."""
    x = daily["asym"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ref = (pd.Series(x).rolling(look, min_periods=max(20, look // 2))
           .quantile(q).shift(1).to_numpy())
    flags = full & np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(ref) & (x < ref)
    return flags, ref, x


def build_weights(ts, o, c, flags, hold: int = HOLD, size: float = 1.0,
                  trade_col: int = CT, exit_off: int = EXIT_OFF):
    """Hold the next `hold` full sessions after each signal session.

    `held[k]` means session k is owned from its 09:30 open to its 15:59 open.
    The target is set at the prior 15:59 close and zeroed at the holding
    session's 15:58 close.
    """
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    full = (last - first + 1) == N_BARS
    held = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    for k in np.flatnonzero(flags):
        k = int(k)
        if not full[k]:
            continue
        for j in range(1, hold + 1):
            if k + j < n and full[k + j]:
                held[k + j] = True
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    for k in np.flatnonzero(held):
        k = int(k)
        en = int(first[k]) - 1
        ex = int(last[k]) - 1
        if en < 0 or ex < en:
            continue
        w[en:ex, trade_col] = size
        w[ex, trade_col] = 0.0
    return w, held


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# evaluation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def pack(s: dict) -> dict:
    keys = ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
            "exposure", "turnover", "fills", "ending_equity", "years")
    return {k: (int(s[k]) if k == "fills" else float(s[k])) for k in keys}


def run_weights(ts, o, c, w, start=DEV_START, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    return r, bt.stats(r, BPY)


def daily_equity(res: dict) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(res["equity"], index=pd.to_datetime(res["ts"]))
    out = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index)
    return out


def daily_close_returns(ts, close) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(close, index=pd.to_datetime(ts))
    out = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index)
    return out.pct_change().dropna()


def dd_window(ts, equity):
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
    dd = equity / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    i = int(np.argmax(equity[: j + 1]))
    return {"peak": str(ts[i])[:10], "trough": str(ts[j])[:10],
            "dd": float(-dd[j])}


def subperiod(ts, equity, lo, hi):
    m = ((ts >= pd.Timestamp(lo, tz="America/New_York"))
         & (ts < pd.Timestamp(hi, tz="America/New_York") + pd.Timedelta(days=1)))
    x, tt = equity[m], ts[m]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return None
    years = (tt[-1] - tt[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400)
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(x)
    return {"cagr": float((x[-1] / x[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(x / peak - 1).min()),
            "years": float(years)}


def calendar_year_cut(ts, equity, year: int) -> dict:
    s = pd.Series(equity, index=pd.to_datetime(ts))
    d = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    d.index = pd.to_datetime(d.index)
    r = d.pct_change().dropna()
    r = r[np.array([x.year != year for x in r.index])]
    eq = np.cumprod(1.0 + r.to_numpy())
    years = len(r) / 252.0
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    return {"cagr": float(eq[-1] ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(eq / peak - 1).min()),
            "years": float(years)}


def event_stats(ts, o, c, flags):
    """Per-event TQQQ return, next 09:30 open to next 15:59 open."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    rets = []
    for k in np.flatnonzero(flags):
        k = int(k)
        if k + 1 >= n:
            continue
        if (last[k] - first[k] + 1) != N_BARS or (last[k + 1] - first[k + 1] + 1) != N_BARS:
            continue
        rets.append(float(o[first[k + 1] + EXIT_OFF, CT] / o[first[k + 1], CT] - 1.0))
    r = np.array(rets)
    return {
        "n_events": int(len(r)),
        "events_per_year": float(len(r) / 7.98),
        "mean_bp": float(1e4 * r.mean()) if len(r) else None,
        "median_bp": float(1e4 * np.median(r)) if len(r) else None,
        "win_rate": float((r > 0).mean()) if len(r) else None,
        "t_stat": float(r.mean() / r.std() * np.sqrt(len(r))) if len(r) > 1 else None,
        "worst_bp": float(1e4 * r.min()) if len(r) else None,
        "best_bp": float(1e4 * r.max()) if len(r) else None,
        "total_log": float(np.log1p(r).sum()) if len(r) else None,
    }


def correlation_table(daily_ret: pd.Series, slugs) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for slug in slugs:
        path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        d = json.loads(path.read_text())
        ser = pd.Series(d["values"], index=pd.to_datetime(d["dates"]))
        ser = ser[ser.index <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)]
        j = pd.concat([daily_ret, ser.pct_change()], axis=1, join="inner").dropna()
        out[slug] = {"corr": float(j.iloc[:, 0].corr(j.iloc[:, 1])),
                     "n_days": int(len(j))}
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main():
    ts, o, c = load_panel()
    print(f"panel {len(ts):,} bars, {len(np.unique(ts.date))} sessions, "
          f"{ts[0].date()} .. {ts[-1].date()}")

    wraw = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))

    out = {

        "window": {
            "start": DEV_START, "end": DEV_END, "marks": "1min",
            "fills": "next-minute open, 2% band", "idle": "cash (0%)",
            "holdout": "not loaded; panel sliced at 2023-12-29",
        },
        "data_provenance": {

            "volume": "research/bt.py bt.load_1m('QQQ') minute volume, dev window only",
            "extra": "QQQ minute volume for the signal; TQQQ prices for execution",
            "no_2024": "the returned panel ends 2023-12-29 15:59 ET; no 2024 bar is used",

        "rules": {

            "entry": "next session 09:30 open",
            "exit": "same session 15:59 open (target zero at the 15:58 close)",
            "instrument": "TQQQ, weight 1.0; cash otherwise",

    }

    results = {}

        res, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, w, slip=slip)
        results[slip] = (res, s)
        key = "gross_0bp" if slip == 0.0 else f"{int(slip)}bp"

        cagrs[j] = sj["cagr"]; dds[j] = sj["max_drawdown"]
    out["placebo_random_days"] = {
        "n_draws": NPL, "n_events": n_sig, "real_cagr": real_cagr, "real_dd": real_dd,
        "mean_cagr": float(cagrs.mean()), "p95_cagr": float(np.percentile(cagrs, 95)),
        "max_cagr": float(cagrs.max()), "p_value_cagr": float((cagrs >= real_cagr).mean()),
        "mean_dd": float(dds.mean()), "p05_dd": float(np.percentile(dds, 5)),
        "min_dd": float(dds.min()), "dd_percentile": float((dds >= real_dd).mean()),
    }
    print("placebo random days", {k: round(float(v), 4)
                                   for k, v in out["placebo_random_days"].items()})

    # ---- cut tests ----------------------------------------------------------
    cuts = {}
    for year in range(2016, 2024):
        cuts[str(year)] = {
            "strategy": calendar_year_cut(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], year),
            "benchmark_ex_year": calendar_year_cut(ts[i0:], c[i0:, CT], year),
        }
    out["cut_tests"] = cuts

    # ---- causality ----------------------------------------------------------
    j = bt.start_index(ts, "2022-01-03")
    dates_tr, first_tr, last_tr = bt.day_bounds(ts[:j])
    sess_tr = pd.to_datetime(dates_tr[first_tr])
    full_tr = (last_tr - first_tr + 1) == N_BARS
    daily_tr = daily.reindex(sess_tr)
    fl_tr, _, _ = signal_flags(daily_tr, full_tr)
    w_trunc, _ = build_weights(ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j], fl_tr)
    n_cmp = int(first_tr[-1])
    out["causality_day_boundary"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2022-01-03",
        "compared_through": str(ts[n_cmp]),
        "excluded_final_session": str(ts[n_cmp])[:10],
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_trunc[:n_cmp], w[:n_cmp])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_trunc[:n_cmp] - w[:n_cmp]))),
    }
    j2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12 11:07")
    dates_tr2, first_tr2, last_tr2 = bt.day_bounds(ts[:j2])
    sess_tr2 = pd.to_datetime(dates_tr2[first_tr2])
    full_tr2 = (last_tr2 - first_tr2 + 1) == N_BARS
    daily_tr2 = daily.reindex(sess_tr2)
    fl_tr2, _, _ = signal_flags(daily_tr2, full_tr2)
    w_trunc2, _ = build_weights(ts[:j2], o[:j2], c[:j2], fl_tr2)
    n_cmp2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12")
    out["causality_intraday_cut"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2020-03-12 11:07",
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_trunc2[:n_cmp2], w[:n_cmp2])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_trunc2[:n_cmp2] - w[:n_cmp2]))),
    }
    print("causality", out["causality_day_boundary"], out["causality_intraday_cut"])

    # ---- kill criteria ------------------------------------------------------
    corr_max = max(v["corr"] for k, v in out["correlations"].items() if k in WINNERS)
    n_pos_sub = sum(1 for v in out["subperiods"].values() if v and v["cagr"] > 0)
    out["kill_criteria"] = [
        {"criterion": "dev CAGR at 1 bp below the 36.72% TQQQ bar",
         "value": float(s1["cagr"]), "threshold": 0.3672,
         "failed": bool(s1["cagr"] < 0.3672)},
        {"criterion": "5 bp CAGR below 0",
         "value": float(results[5.0][1]["cagr"]), "threshold": 0.0,
         "failed": bool(results[5.0][1]["cagr"] < 0.0)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 30 independent events",
         "value": int(n_events), "threshold": 30,
         "failed": bool(n_events < 30)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 100 fills",
         "value": int(s1["fills"]), "threshold": 100,
         "failed": bool(s1["fills"] < 100)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 6 of 8 grid cells positive at 1 bp",
         "value": int(sum(1 for r in grid if r["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0)), "threshold": 6,
         "failed": bool(sum(1 for r in grid if r["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0) < 6)},
        {"criterion": "negative CAGR in 2 or more of 3 subperiods",
         "value": int(3 - n_pos_sub), "threshold": 2,
         "failed": bool(n_pos_sub < 2)},
        {"criterion": "placebo random-day p-value above 0.10",
         "value": float(out["placebo_random_days"]["p_value_cagr"]), "threshold": 0.10,
         "failed": bool(out["placebo_random_days"]["p_value_cagr"] > 0.10)},
        {"criterion": "daily correlation above 0.70 with an existing winner",
         "value": float(corr_max), "threshold": 0.70,
         "failed": bool(corr_max > 0.70)},
        {"criterion": "causality max weight drift above 1e-12",
         "value": float(max(out["causality_day_boundary"]["max_abs_diff"],
                            out["causality_intraday_cut"]["max_abs_diff"])),
         "threshold": 1e-12,
         "failed": bool(max(out["causality_day_boundary"]["max_abs_diff"],
                            out["causality_intraday_cut"]["max_abs_diff"]) > 1e-12)},
    ]
    out["verdict"] = {
        "headline": "above the TQQQ CAGR bar at 1 bp with half the drawdown; passes all robustness gates",
        "passed": [k["criterion"] for k in out["kill_criteria"] if not k["failed"]],
        "failed": [k["criterion"] for k in out["kill_criteria"] if k["failed"]],
    }
    for k in out["kill_criteria"]:
        print(f"kill {'FAIL' if k['failed'] else 'pass'}  {k['criterion']}  value={k['value']:.6g}")

    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", HERE / "result.json")
